plan.name: Workin
plan.title: Six-week calisthenics and resistance-band block
plan.focus: Balanced strength and muscle development with pull-up specialization, scalable dip and pike practice, complete back and leg work, cardio, mobility, and recovery.
plan.reviewBasis: Derived from the consensus-approved Workin V2 plan, then modified at the user's request by replacing Bulgarian split squats with walking lunges and adding one bonus movement to each strength day.

dataProvenance.generatedFrom: The authoritative Workin workout data and the trainee details supplied by the user.
dataProvenance.verification: Personal details and performance are user-reported; this is not a medical assessment or independently verified technique review.
dataProvenance.sensitiveDataNotice: This file contains personal health, body, training, lifestyle, and nutrition information. Share it only with reviewers or systems you trust.

trainingBackground.history: Intermittent training for several years, commonly one or two months of training followed by long breaks.
trainingBackground.recentConsistency: Completed the previous four-week Workin block after approximately one month of consistent training beforehand.
trainingBackground.previousBlockRecovery: The previous workload was manageable and overall strength noticeably improved.

currentPerformance.parallelBarDips: Difficult; requires foot or band assistance

primary: Increase strict pull-ups from approximately 3 toward a long-term target of 20 or more
Build strength and muscle while developing a wider, more complete back
Improve shoulders, upper chest, triceps, dips, and pike pressing
wholeBody: Leg, hamstring, glute, calf, and core development
Scapular control and proportionate posture-related training
goals.bodyComposition: Maintain roughly the same body weight, reduce fat slightly, and gain muscle.

health.note: No reported injury is not equivalent to medical screening or clearance.

equipment.bandCalibration: Brand and actual resistance are unverified; log the specific band, length, anchor, and setup.

nutrition.recentTargetDuration: Approximately two weeks when first reported
nutrition.priorProteinIntake: Much lower according to the user

planRules.progression: Keep assistance, band, leverage, ROM, and setup consistent. Progress only after reaching the listed trigger with clean technique in two comparable sessions. Change one variable, then return to the lower end of the range.
planRules.safety: Stop when ROM or position deteriorates. Sharp, escalating, unstable, radiating, or joint-specific pain is a stop signal. Persistent symptoms, trauma, neurologic symptoms, chest pain, or fainting require qualified assessment.
planRules.moderateAerobic: Zone 2 should feel about 3–4/10: steady breathing while still able to speak in complete sentences. Replace intervals with Zone 2 whenever leg fatigue compromises Friday or Monday strength performance.

weekGuidance.label: Standardize
weekGuidance.guidance: Use about 3 RIR on compounds while learning the new exercise order, assistance, band setups, and geometry.

weekGuidance.label: Build reps
weekGuidance.guidance: Use the listed RIR. Add reps inside the current ranges where technique and recovery remain stable.

weekGuidance.label: Progress
weekGuidance.guidance: Keep building within the ranges. Saturday uses the first interval session unless leg fatigue calls for Zone 2.

weekGuidance.label: Repeat well
weekGuidance.guidance: Do not change exercises for novelty. Confirm repeatable progress triggers and keep Saturday at Zone 2.

weekGuidance.label: Confirm
weekGuidance.guidance: Complete the final normal week. Progress only where the full trigger is met; choose Zone 2 if recovery is reduced.

weekGuidance.label: Reduce + retest
weekGuidance.guidance: Use the reduced prescriptions, stay near 3 RIR, and complete the standardized reassessment without extra max tests.

pullUp.work: Strength sets plus submaximal endurance work
Harder strength work plus controlled density work

pike: Choose a high-hand position permitting 3×6 at 2 RIR.
Progress feet-elevated pikes after 3×8 with controlled deep ROM.
Add wall-supported partial-ROM work only with pain-free wrist and shoulder tolerance.
dip: Use support holds 3×15–30 sec if a stable support cannot be held.
Build foot-assisted dips to 3×8–10 at 2 RIR.
Build band-assisted dips to 3×8, then use a lighter band.
Accumulate 5–8 clean strict singles before building strict sets from 3×3 toward 3×8–10.

fatigueAndAdjustmentRules: Week 1 uses about 3 RIR on compounds while setup is standardized.
Weeks 2–5 use the listed RIR and progression triggers.
Week 6 reduces working sets by about 40%, stays near 3 RIR, and includes reassessment.
Missed sessions are skipped; sessions are never combined.
If performance declines across two sessions, joint irritation increases, or soreness persists beyond about 72 hours, reduce working sets by 30–40% for one week.
Do not progress pull-up, dip, and pike difficulty simultaneously.

retestProtocol.timing: Baseline before Week 1 and repeat during Week 6 with identical assistance, equipment, and geometry.
sessionA: One clean set of the current pike progression, capped at 12
One clean set of the current dip progression, capped at 10; record assistance
One clean ring-row set, capped at 20; record ring and foot position
sessionBAtLeast48HoursLater: One standardized walking-lunge set per leg, capped at 20 steps per leg
One clean hanging-knee-raise set, capped at 15
retestProtocol.separateDay: Twelve-minute walk/run test; record distance using the same location and similar conditions.
retestProtocol.stopRule: End every test when ROM or body position deteriorates.

days.title: Strength A
days.summary: Priority pull-up and dip practice, balanced by horizontal pulling, unilateral legs, a hinge, and direct shoulder and arm work.

exercises.name: Standard strength warm-up
exercises.cue: Brisk walk/jog 2–3 min; wrist rocks ×8; scapular pulls ×6; scapular push-ups ×8; squats ×10; then one easy rehearsal set for the first push, pull, and leg movement.

exercises.name: Strict pull-up
exercises.cue: 1–2 RIR · Complete 4×2 clean twice and confirm a 4–5 rep maximum in Week 6 before advancing. Use assistance if later sets lose full ROM.

exercises.name: Foot- or band-assisted dip
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Complete 3×8 twice, then reduce assistance slightly. Stop for shoulder or sternum pain.

exercises.name: Walking lunge
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Count steps per leg, not total. After 3×14 per leg twice, add band resistance rather than continually adding steps.

exercises.name: Ring row
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Complete 3×12 twice, then lower the rings or move the feet forward while keeping the body rigid.

exercises.name: Band Romanian deadlift
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Complete 3×15, then increase band tension or use a staggered stance. Keep the hinge controlled.

exercises.name: Band lateral raise
exercises.cue: 1–2 RIR · Complete 3×20 without shrugging, then increase tension. Pair with the RDL.

exercises.name: Band hammer curl
exercises.cue: 1–2 RIR · Complete 2×20 with still upper arms, then increase tension. Pair with triceps extensions.

exercises.name: Band overhead triceps extension
exercises.cue: BONUS · 1–2 RIR. Complete 2×20, then increase tension; use a band pressdown if the overhead position is uncomfortable.

exercises.name: Pallof press
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Secure the band to a stall bar. Complete 2×15 without trunk rotation, then increase resistance.

days.title: Zone 2 + mobility
days.summary: Build aerobic capacity without compromising Wednesday’s strength work, then complete a short whole-body mobility sequence.

exercises.name: Zone 2 walk or walk/jog
exercises.cue: Use a pace that lets you speak in complete sentences. Add about 5 minutes only when strength-session recovery remains normal.

exercises.name: Thoracic rotation
exercises.cue: Move slowly through a comfortable range without forcing the end position.

exercises.name: Stall-bar chest stretch
exercises.cue: Use a gentle stretch and keep the shoulder below a painful range.

exercises.name: Wall slide
exercises.cue: Keep ribs controlled and use only the range where the forearms remain comfortable.

exercises.name: Ankle dorsiflexion rock
exercises.cue: Keep the heel down and guide the knee over the toes without collapsing the arch.

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hip-flexor stretch
exercises.cue: Gently tuck the pelvis and avoid arching the lower back.

days.title: Strength B
days.eyebrow: Pull-up volume · pike press · upper chest
days.summary: Assisted pulling volume and scalable vertical pressing lead a full-body session with upper-chest, hamstring, rear-shoulder, calf, and core work.

exercises.name: Standard strength warm-up
exercises.cue: Brisk walk/jog 2–3 min; wrist rocks ×8; scapular pulls ×6; scapular push-ups ×8; squats ×10; then one easy rehearsal set for the first push, pull, and leg movement.

exercises.name: Band-assisted pull-up
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Use the same inspected band and setup for every set. Complete 3×10 twice, then use a lighter band.

exercises.name: Elevated-hand pike push-up
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Choose a support height that permits full reps. Complete 3×10 twice, then lower the support slightly.

exercises.name: Feet-elevated push-up
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Complete 3×12 twice, then elevate the feet slightly or add band resistance. Pair with lunges.

exercises.name: Reverse lunge
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Complete 3×12 per leg, then add band resistance or a deeper controlled ROM.

exercises.name: Ring hamstring curl
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Complete 3×12, then move the feet farther away or elevate them. Regress to glute-bridge walkouts 3×6–10.

exercises.name: Band face pull to external rotation
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Use a secure stall-bar anchor. Complete 3×20 with scapular control, then increase tension.

exercises.name: Single-leg calf raise
exercises.cue: 1–2 RIR · Complete 4×20, then add band resistance. Use support for balance.

exercises.name: Wall tibialis raise
exercises.cue: BONUS · 1–2 RIR. Keep heels down and avoid rocking. Move the feet farther from the wall after 2×25.

exercises.name: Hollow-body regression
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Reach 30 seconds twice with the lower back controlled, then lengthen the limb position.

days.title: Recovery
days.summary: Let the priority movements recover. Walking and gentle mobility are optional, not another training session.

exercises.name: Easy walk
exercises.cue: Finish feeling better than you started. Do not turn this into a conditioning session.

exercises.name: Gentle mobility
exercises.cue: Choose comfortable hip, ankle, chest, and shoulder movements. No additional pull-ups, pikes, dips, or leg training.

days.title: Strength C
days.intensity: Technique work at 2–3 reps in reserve
days.summary: Low-fatigue skill practice supports the main pull-up, dip, and pike sessions while rows, squats, shoulders, triceps, and core round out the week.

exercises.name: Standard strength warm-up
exercises.cue: Brisk walk/jog 2–3 min; wrist rocks ×8; scapular pulls ×6; scapular push-ups ×8; squats ×10; then one easy rehearsal set for the first push, pull, and leg movement.

exercises.name: Strict pull-up technique singles
exercises.cue: About 2 RIR · Progress to 5×2 only after the tested maximum reaches about five clean repetitions.

exercises.name: Assisted dip technique
exercises.cue: 3 RIR · Use more assistance than Monday. Complete 2×10 smoothly, then reduce assistance slightly on Friday only.

exercises.name: Elevated-hand pike push-up technique
exercises.cue: 3 RIR · Keep this easier than Wednesday. Progress the exercise level only through Wednesday’s primary sets.

exercises.name: Ring row
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Complete 3×15 twice, then lower the rings or move the feet forward. Pair with front squats.

exercises.name: Band front squat
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Complete 3×15, then increase tension while preserving depth and trunk position.

exercises.name: Band lateral raise
exercises.cue: 1–2 RIR · Complete 2×20 without shrugging, then increase tension. Pair with close-grip push-ups.

exercises.name: Elevated close-grip push-up
exercises.cue: 2–3 RIR · Hands just inside shoulder width. Complete 2×10 twice, then lower the support; a narrower diamond is optional after floor 2×10.

exercises.name: Hanging knee raise
exercises.cue: 2 RIR · Avoid swinging. Complete 3×12, then raise the knees higher or gradually straighten the legs.

exercises.name: Side plank
exercises.cue: BONUS · About 2 RIR. Keep the hips stacked. After two controlled 40-second holds, lengthen the lever.

days.title: Cardio
days.summary: Most Saturdays extend the aerobic base; two controlled interval sessions add a small higher-intensity exposure.

exercises.name: Saturday conditioning
exercises.cue: Weeks 1, 2, 4: Zone 2. Weeks 3, 5: 8-min warm-up, 6×1 min at RPE 8/10 with 2 min easy, then 5-min cooldown. Week 6: easy Zone 2.

weekPrescriptions.3: 8-min warm-up + 6 × 1 min hard / 2 min easy + 5-min cooldown
weekPrescriptions.5: 8-min warm-up + 6 × 1 min hard / 2 min easy + 5-min cooldown

exercises.name: Comfortable cooldown mobility
exercises.cue: Use calm, pain-free movements for whichever areas feel restricted after the week.

days.title: Complete rest
days.summary: Sunday is not a missed-workout replacement day. Normal light movement is fine; begin the next week fresh.

exercises.name: Rest from planned training
exercises.cue: A casual walk is fine, but it is not required and does not need to be intense.

exercises.name: Two-minute weekly review
exercises.cue: Record pain, energy, completed reps, band setups, and any performance decline.
